title:
PROPORTION,
(INVERSE PROPORTION)
objective: LO: I can solve problems involving inverse proportion.

content.text: Inverse proportion means as one quantity increases, the other decreases at the same rate. If one doubles, the other halves.
Formula: y ∝ 1/x gives y = k/x. The product xy = k is always constant.

examples.expr: 4 workers take 6 hours; 8 workers take 3 hours
If one halves, the other halves too

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: For inverse proportion, y = k/x. Find k by multiplying: k = x × y.
key_idea.equation: y = k ÷ x → k = x × y
key_idea.caption: The product of x and y is always constant

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – finding k
modelled_examples.question: y is inversely proportional to x. When x = 4, y = 9. Find k.
modelled_examples.explanation: For inverse proportion, multiply x and y to find k.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – using the formula
modelled_examples.question: Using y = 36/x, find y when x = 12.
modelled_examples.explanation: Substitute into the formula and divide.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – workers problem
modelled_examples.question: 6 workers build a wall in 10 days. How long for 15 workers?
modelled_examples.explanation: More workers means fewer days (inverse relationship).

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – speed-time
modelled_examples.question: A journey takes 3 hours at 60 mph. How long at 90 mph?
modelled_examples.explanation: The distance (product) stays constant; faster speed means less time.

items.statement: In inverse proportion, the product xy is constant
More workers means a job takes less time (inverse proportion)
If x doubles and y doubles, this is inverse proportion
The graph of y = k/x is a curve that never touches the axes

problems.text: A farmer has enough feed to last 12 cows for 20 days. The farmer buys 4 more cows. How many days will the feed now last?
The intensity of light I is inversely proportional to the square of the distance d from the source. At d = 2 m, I = 100 units. Find I at d = 5 m.
